sections.title: The Sovereignty of God
observations: This section emphasizes the majesty and sovereignty of God as the King who reigns over all the earth. The psalmist calls the nations to tremble before Him, highlighting His supreme authority and power.
The imagery of God sitting enthroned between the cherubim signifies His presence among His people and His role as the divine ruler. It invites worship and reverence from all creation.

sections.title: God's Holiness and Justice
observations: The psalmist declares God's holiness, which is a central theme in the worship of Israel. God's holiness sets Him apart from all other beings and demands a response of awe and reverence.

The mention of God's justice and righteousness reinforces the idea that He is not only powerful but also good. His reign is characterized by fairness and equity, which is a source of comfort for His people.

sections.title: God's Faithfulness to His People
observations: The psalmist recalls the historical acts of God, particularly His dealings with Moses, Aaron, and Samuel. This remembrance serves to remind the people of God's faithfulness and responsiveness to their cries.
The call to worship is rooted in the acknowledgment of God's past actions, encouraging the community to trust in His continued faithfulness.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord reigns; let the peoples tremble! He sits enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth quake!
Exalt the Lord our God; worship at his footstool! Holy is he!
Exalt the Lord our God, and worship at his holy mountain; for the Lord our God is holy!

questions: What does it mean for God to reign, and how should that affect our daily lives?
How can we better understand the holiness of God in our worship?
In what ways can we remember and celebrate God's faithfulness in our own lives?
